articles.title: Burkina Faso moves to decolonize education through curriculum reform
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Burkina Faso has begun reviewing its history, geography and civic education curricula. The government says the aim is to “decolonize” the country’s schools by removing colonial-era portrayals of African history and giving more space to national history, African resistance, cultural values, and local knowledge. Speaking during a meeting with education officials in Ouagadougou, Secondary Education Minister Moumouni Zoungrana criticized the language used in school textbooks to describe European colonialists. “Those who came to conquer Africa are called explorers, conquerors. Were they conquerors? They were spies…. They were invaders,” the minister said, according to APA News . articles.content_excerpt: Thousands participated in a joint delegation of opposition groups in India who were attempting to meet the Chief Justice (CJI) of the country on Monday, October 12. articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: High school and university students in France continued their protests on Tuesday, October 13, demanding government investment in public education. Police used tear gas and dispersal grenades on crowds, including at Tuesday’s central march in Paris.
